spokenText: Welcome home. Here is your briefing for Saturday, the fourteenth of November. First, the kwacha. According to the Bank of Zambia, the kwacha closed Friday at an average of twenty point four four kwacha to the US dollar, with banks buying at about twenty point four two and selling at twenty point four seven. That's slightly weaker than Tuesday's twenty point four zero, so the kwacha has slipped roughly zero point two percent this week. The Bank's next monetary policy announcement is on the twenty-seventh of November. Your email. I'm afraid I couldn't read your inbox this time. The Gmail connection has expired and needs to be signed in again under your Claude connector settings. Once that's done, I'll summarise this week's mail and flag what needs your attention. Your calendar is clear. There are no events or appointments between now and the end of January. And finally, Tayant Pay. The August tab of the Phoenix Tayant transaction records shows ninety-five transactions processed between the third and the thirty-first of August, across twenty-three trading days. About eighty-one of those were customer transfers, and fourteen were internal movements such as mega transfers, liquidity withdrawals and director loans. On the Zambian side, revenue was one thousand, one hundred and fourteen kwacha, fees were two hundred and thirty-eight kwacha, leaving a profit of about eight hundred and seventy-seven kwacha. The Russian ledger earned roughly twelve thousand, two hundred roubles in revenue. One thing to note: the August tab also carries September to November entries, so the totals at the top of the sheet cover more than just August. That's everything for now.
